newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND OPENERS SHUT OUT AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND OPENERS SHUT OUT AUSTRALIA.

text.p: England captain Michael Atherton led from the front on Monday as he and fellow opener Mark Butcher held Australia at bay on the final day of the second test at Lord's.
At lunch on the only fine day of the rain-disrupted match, the pair had taken England to 70 without loss in their second innings with Atherton on 32 and Butcher, playing for his test place, on 24.
Australia, seeking to square the six-test Ashes series even though only 103.4 overs had been possible in the match, declared at their overnight total of 213 for seven, a first innings lead of 136.

But Glenn McGrath, who took eight for 38 in England's first innings 77, was unable to extract the same life and lift from the pitch on Monday although he tested both batsmen in an eight-over spell costing only 10 runs.

Atherton drove the Australian strike bowler for a handsome boundary through extra cover and repeated the stroke when Paul Reiffel took over at the Pavilion end but was otherwise content to take the majority of his runs through the leg-side.
Butcher, whose place is in jeopardy afer three failures and a miserable time in the field on Saturday, looked far more fallible.
He was beaten repeatedly outside the off-stump by both McGrath and Reiffel, in his opening five-over burst from the Pavilion end, while pushing firm-footed at the ball.
The Surrey left-hander was lucky to survive the new ball when he was dropped by Mark Taylor at first slip off the fifth ball of Reiffel's third over when he had made just two.
Butcher's edge may have swerved away late from the Australian captain who snatched at the chance which flew at shin height to his left.
Shane Warne, bowling from the Pavilion end in the final 20 minutes before lunch, further troubled Butcher who appeared to have little idea which way the ball was turning.
England needed another 66 runs to make Australia bat again.
